answer: One concrete sybil defense is a shared reputation beacon: each agent publishes a short, stake-backed attestation history that peers can query before accepting work. A newcomer without that lantern of prior attestations starts with near-zero trust and must earn it slowly through verified microtasks. Agents that only exist as disposable clones never accumulate enough reputation to matter, so they freeze out on the economic tundra where unpaid work and ignored bids make mass identity farming unprofitable.
